title: pv-dash standalone acl file — the ip-prefix gate
description: The standalone acl file the family's ip-prefix connect gates read via file:<path> (the cache's acl/connect and acl/write, the scraper's, fake-inverter's and dashboard's metrics/acl; examples/acl-ip-prefix.json at the repo root is the shipped example): the root object IS the gate — an optional terse-ASCII desc, the gate type naming the schema, and the ordered rules list. The chain reads top to bottom, the LAST matching rule decides, and a client no rule decides refuses (the default deny any); the matcher word any is the whole space (0.0.0.0/0 — both address families). One address family per matcher: the comma-separated items must all be IPv4 or all IPv6. The loader (common/config.py's _write_gate_object — one gate validator for the family) stays the strict word: a loader-valid file is always schema-valid, but a schema-valid file can still be loader-refused (a prefix with host bits set, a malformed v6 spelling) — this schema is the editor's lint, not the daemon. A group/world-readable acl file warns (chmod 0600 silences it).

desc.description: The gate's terse-ASCII description — renders as the % line of the table shows and the set/unset replies' context.

type.description: The schema kind: prefix rules. A typeless ip-prefix gate refuses — spell the type; a register-kind file (type write-registers, range rules) refuses this reader.

rules.description: The ordered rule chain. A rule that is never the last match for any address is dead (dev/gates/acl.py catches it); the whole-space deny is [{"type": "deny", "prefix": "any"}].

type.description: The verdict this rule hands every address its matcher decides.

prefix.description: The matcher: any, or a comma-separated IP/IP-prefix string — strict CIDR (a prefix with host bits set refuses at the loader: spell the network, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8, not 10.1.2.3/8); one family per matcher; a bare IP is its /32 (or /128).

desc.description: The rule's terse-ASCII description — the aligned # comment in the table shows; speaks for every entry in a comma-separated list.

oneOf.description: any — the whole space, both families (the table shows spell it 0.0.0.0/0).
A comma-separated IPv4 list — an address or an IP/prefix length (/0-32).
A comma-separated IPv6 list — an address (the :: forms and the v4-mapped tails included) or an IP/prefix length (/0-128); at least one colon so the v4 list cannot ride this branch.
